chapter_mission: Ben takes command. Sera's conditional trust activates — 'Tell me where to stand, Skywalker' — repeating the Gavran pattern she cannot yet see she is repeating. Team synthesis reveals Veraine's project: a network-wide amplification array. Ben files Gavran's note about lattice resonance between disparate traditions without yet understanding what he has found.
chapter_turn: Ben stops reacting to the crisis and starts setting its terms. That authority is real and earned, and it is also the exact shape of the trap: Sera is following him the way she followed Gavran. The book's antidote to the Skywalker trap (synthesis instead of unilateral command) is planted here as an archival footnote Ben does not yet read as a solution.

scene_plan.purpose: Common area reconfigured as tactical briefing. Ben lays out the intercept strategy — skip ahead of Veraine rather than follow. His mother's cadence in his voice without him meaning it. Sera straightens her spine, shifts from adversarial to subordinate. 'Tell me where to stand, Skywalker.' The last person she chose to follow sealed her in a wall. H13 advances.

Evidence from every node spread across every flat surface. Sera pins Corridor maps to the bulkhead. Desh's tactical eye, Sera's historical vocabulary, Torin's Force-theoretical expertise, Kael's dry corrections — for the first time, the group synthesises rather than stalemates. The pattern resolves: each repurposed node is another antenna. Veraine is not attacking the seal, she is inverting its architecture.

Ben's workspace. Scrolling Gavran's marginalia on the Codex data, searching for counter-measures, he finds it: 'Ankhural theorised that the lattice could be reinforced through harmonic resonance between disparate traditions. We lacked the will or the trust to attempt it.' Sera frowns at Ankhural's name. Ben bookmarks the note and moves on. H14 plants. The solution exists. Nobody in the room recognises it.

relationship_turns.to: conditional command — Sera has offered Ben the kind of trust she gave Gavran. The gift is also a test. She does not yet know Ben will pass it by refusing to be Gavran
commander — the synthesis in s2 is the first time the group has produced an answer no single member could reach. Ben ran the room, but the answer belonged to everyone
named correspondent — the resonance note is Gavran speaking directly to a successor he did not know he would have. Ben registers the voice without registering the message

exit_vector: The Steady Returns on the intercept vector, ship configured for the attack phase. Ben at the tactical display, Sera watching him with the investment that is both gift and warning. Gavran's resonance note bookmarked on Ben's datapad, filed under 'return later' — a label Ben has used before for things that turned out to be the answer.
notes: Brooks 'attack phase' begins here. Ben's assumption of command is the Act 3 opening beat and must feel earned — the chapter should land him as *capable of commanding this team* even while the reader registers Sera's gift as Gavran's pattern in miniature. The synthesis scene in s2 is a scene-level foreshadow of the climactic solution: disparate traditions producing an answer none could reach alone. Do not italicise it. Gavran's note in s3 is Chekhov at full tension — the reader must register its weight before Ben does. Voice: Zahn-procedural throughout; Allston-warmth permitted in s2 briefly; Stover-permitted in s3 for one interior beat as Ben reads Gavran's handwriting. Anti-patterns: (a) do not let Ben articulate the Gavran parallel about himself yet — that belongs to Ch18; (b) Sera's 'Tell me where to stand' must land without her seeing what she is saying; (c) the resonance note must not be read aloud by any character. Ben's eyes on the page; a silent file.
